issues.description: RabbitMQ host, queue names, and port numbers are hardcoded in source files. This makes it difficult to deploy to different environments without code changes.
issues.remediation: Externalize configuration to application.properties or environment variables. Consider using Spring configuration or Azure App Configuration.

issues.issue: RabbitMQ dependency requires migration to Azure Service Bus
issues.description: Application uses RabbitMQ for messaging. For Azure deployment, this should be migrated to Azure Service Bus or containerized RabbitMQ on AKS.
issues.remediation: Migrate to Azure Service Bus for managed messaging, or deploy RabbitMQ on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS).

issues.issue: Jetty embedded server requires containerization strategy
issues.description: Application uses Jetty Maven plugin for local development. For Azure deployment, consider containerizing with Docker or deploying to Azure App Service.
issues.remediation: Create Dockerfile for containerized deployment to Azure App Service or AKS. Alternatively, package as standard WAR for Azure App Service.

issues.issue: WebSocket support in Azure App Service
issues.description: Application uses WebSocket for real-time communication. Azure App Service requires specific configuration to support WebSocket connections.
issues.remediation: Enable WebSocket support in Azure App Service configuration. Consider using Azure SignalR Service for better scalability.

issues.description: RabbitMQ host and queue name are hardcoded. This makes it difficult to connect to different RabbitMQ instances in different environments.
issues.remediation: Use environment variables or configuration files for connection settings.

issues.issue: RabbitMQ client needs Azure Service Bus migration
issues.description: Client application connects to RabbitMQ. For Azure deployment, migrate to Azure Service Bus SDK.
issues.remediation: Replace RabbitMQ AMQP client with Azure Service Bus Java SDK. Update connection logic to use Azure Service Bus connection strings.

dependencies.name: com.rabbitmq:amqp-client
dependencies.recommendation: Migrate to Azure Service Bus Java SDK (com.azure:azure-messaging-servicebus)

dependencies.name: javax.websocket:javax.websocket-api
dependencies.recommendation: Consider Azure SignalR Service for better scalability

dependencies.name: org.eclipse.jetty:jetty-maven-plugin
dependencies.recommendation: Package as WAR for Azure App Service or containerize with Docker

recommendations.recommendation: Migrate from RabbitMQ to Azure Service Bus
recommendations.rationale: Azure Service Bus provides fully managed enterprise message broker with message queues and publish-subscribe topics. This eliminates the need to manage RabbitMQ infrastructure.
steps: 1. Create Azure Service Bus namespace in Azure portal
2. Create queue or topic based on application needs
3. Replace amqp-client dependency with azure-messaging-servicebus
4. Update RabbitMQConsumer to use Service Bus Receiver
5. Update democlient to use Service Bus Sender
6. Test message flow end-to-end

recommendations.rationale: Hardcoded configuration prevents deployment flexibility and follows cloud anti-patterns. Azure provides multiple configuration management options.
steps: 1. Create application.properties or use environment variables
2. Replace hardcoded values with configuration lookups
3. Set up Azure App Configuration or Key Vault for production
4. Update deployment scripts to inject configuration

recommendations.rationale: Containerization provides consistent deployment across environments and enables deployment to Azure App Service, AKS, or Azure Container Instances.
steps: 1. Create Dockerfile for the demo WAR application
2. Use Tomcat or Jetty base image
3. Build and test container locally
4. Push to Azure Container Registry
5. Deploy to Azure App Service or AKS

recommendations.recommendation: Evaluate Azure SignalR Service for WebSocket
recommendations.rationale: Azure SignalR Service provides managed real-time messaging with automatic scaling and better performance for WebSocket connections.
steps: 1. Create Azure SignalR Service instance
2. Evaluate migration effort from raw WebSocket to SignalR
3. Update client-side code to use SignalR JavaScript client
4. Update server-side code to use SignalR Java SDK

recommendations.recommendation: Consider upgrading from Java 1.8 to Java 11 or 17 LTS
recommendations.rationale: Java 8 is becoming dated. Azure fully supports Java 11 and 17 LTS versions with better performance and security features.
steps: 1. Update pom.xml compiler source and target versions
2. Test application with newer Java version
3. Address any compatibility issues
4. Update Azure App Service runtime configuration

recommended.purpose: Replace RabbitMQ with managed message broker
